scope: Read-only mathematical proof, source and recorded result inspection. No component, ray, action, reference or inverse rerun.
findings: The exact positive-part integral includes same-sign and sign-changing coupled endpoint directions; independent polynomial splitting tests the same algebra.
The supporting-slope inequality is valid only for the stated convex jump. Adding a polar-cone normal weakens the linear lower bound with the correct sign.
The c=3A/8 example has positive signed coordinate probes yet a negative joint direction; coordinate-only stationarity is insufficient.
The c=A/5 example has a nonzero optimal constant-support residual but exact zero half-segment support; restricted-support failure is inconclusive, and minus that residual need not be descent.
The reversed cusp is correctly rejected by the convex-support construction rather than hidden by a zero averaged gradient.
The native tangent residual is reconstructed from preserved identified evidence; its existing action decrease and failed local flag are retained rather than relabeled.
limitations: The analytic proof concerns the unchanged retained-node directional functional under convex-jump assumptions, not a global first arrival or inserted knots.
The exact component cases use constant face coefficients. General variable-coefficient integration needs a separate error bound.
Internal-node stationarity alone does not establish a consistent source/model derivative or resolve branch switches; the proof states the missing joint envelope argument.
Native residual reconstruction uses saved floating-point diagnostics and previously checked finite action decreases; this reviewer did not recompute them.
